thread:
ana: quick QA on the model catalog shelf + compare table — found a few small but annoying behaviors when pinning versions. tagging @kim for design, @michael for eng. :eyes:

michael: can you repro? steps?

ana: yep. steps: open catalog, select two models, click Compare, then pin the older version on the left row. keyboard focus jumps to the top of the page and the compare panel scrolls weirdly. happens on Win+Chrome and mac safari.

jordan: interesting. does the pinned state change the DOM order? might be a virtualization/scroll anchor issue.

ana: I inspected — pin toggle moves a `.pinned` element to the top of the compare table for visual grouping (intended), but we don't preserve the active element ref. quick snippet of problematic pattern: 

```
// pseudo
if (model.isPinned) {
  table.prepend(row)
}
// we lose focus here
```

kim: oof. visually nice but accessibility problem. recommendation: keep DOM order stable and use CSS to visually group/anchor pinned rows, or restore focus after move.

michael: agree. prefer stable DOM + CSS transform. restoring focus is a fallback. also concerned about screen readers announcing sudden content reflows — we should avoid removing nodes.

ana: for SRs we tried adding `aria-live` regions but it double-announces when the compare diff updates. current quick patch I tested: `aria-hidden` the temp moved node and announce a single summary in an `aria-live="polite"` element. feels hacky.

design-bot: suggestion: keep visual pin at top via a clone (display-only) + keep original row in DOM (hidden visually). ensures a11y + keyboard continuity.

jordan: clone approach might duplicate tab stops unless we ensure the clone is inert (`aria-hidden` and `tabindex=-1`). also need to maintain hover interactions mapping to original.

kim: design decision: do we want pinned rows to be the canonical interactive rows or purely visual anchors? if canonical, keyboard should jump to the pinned instance. if visual-only, pinned state is purely an indicator and keyboard should stay with original.

michael: engineering preference: canonical is simpler for click targets and permalinks, but we must then avoid DOM moves that steal focus. Could implement smooth scroll+focus transfer rather than reparenting.

ana: another tiny nit — performance badge tooltip overflows the compare panel when pinned. tooltip arrow gets clipped. easy CSS fix: ensure tooltip portal mounts to body or has `overflow: visible` on container.

kim: noted. copy tweak for the pin affordance? current label says "Pin version" but some folks read it as pinning the compare set not a model version. maybe "Pin this model version to compare" is too long. alternatives?

jordan: shorter: "Pin version for compare" or use an icon + hover text only. keep primary label concise in mobile.

ana: also accessibility nit: keyboard nav should announce pinned state change, e.g., "Pinned - v1.2.3". we should use `role="status"` or update `aria-live` ephemeral text on toggle.

michael: will prototype two fixes: (A) keep DOM stable + visual clone for pinned anchor; (B) if canonical move is needed, implement focus preservation and explicit `aria-live` summary.

kim: from design: prefer stable DOM. also add microcopy: on hover/tooltip: "Pinned — this version will remain visible in comparisons". shorter copy for the button: "Pin".

ana: QA notes: i'll run keyboard SR tests after PR. also repro: weird focus when using compare keyboard shortcuts (g then c). attaching mini gif in thread. :thumbsup:

michael: thanks. @design-bot can you add the copy change to the catalog copy doc?

design-bot: added: catalog/copy/pins.md — line: "Pin — Keep a model version visible in compare views. Hover for details."

jordan: one last thought — perf badges: consider a numeric tooltip that includes percentile ("p50 120ms, p95 420ms") rather than just an icon to reduce clicks. also accessible text for color indicators: provide `aria-label` like "Latency: p95 420ms".

kim: love that. final: i'll update the design spec and generate a small a11y checklist for the PR. thanks all.

ana: will follow up with screenshots and clipboard of the CSS patch for tooltip portal.

michael: i'll start a branch and @ana for review. leaving this thread open for followups.
